cards.text: Friend, nobody signs this psalm, but it opens LOUD: "Hallelujah!" The psalmist says it's good to sing praises to our God, and pleasant and lovely to praise Him. Then come the reasons, handed out like cookies fresh off the tray.

cards.question: The psalmist's first reason to praise: the LORD builds up ___.

cards.text: He gathers the exiles of Israel too, people far from home. Friend, I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer, so getting gathered back up is my FAVORITE kind of news.

cards.question: The LORD gathers the people who were scattered. Then the psalm gets close and personal. What does He do for the brokenhearted?

cards.text: He binds up their wounds too. Then the psalm looks UP, from one broken heart to the whole night sky, where the LORD determines the number of the stars.

cards.question: God knows exactly how many stars there are. What else does the psalm say He does with every one of them?

answers.text: He calls each one by name
He lights each one at dusk
He moves each one by hand

cards.text: Every single star, by NAME. I named six toppings after my six kids, and I STILL call the sprinkles "Chip" half the time.

cards.question: Naming every star says something about God. True or false: the psalm says His understanding has a limit somewhere.
Then the psalm sets two kinds of people side by side. The LORD sustains the ___, but casts the ___ to the ground.

cards.text: Then the song circles back with a fresh call to praise. This psalmist is like my oven timer, friend: you think it's done, and it goes off AGAIN.

cards.question: This second call to praise comes with something extra. How does the psalmist say to sing to the LORD?

cards.text: Get the harp out and make music to our God. He's the God who covers the sky with clouds and prepares rain for the earth.

cards.question: Clouds roll in and rain comes down. Then up on the hills, God makes ___ grow.
God provides food for the animals. Then the psalm points to some little ones who call out, and He feeds them too. Who are they?

cards.text: The young ravens call, and God feeds them. I used to call out from the back of that junk drawer, and the only answer I ever got was the dead batteries arguing about who had the most charge left.

cards.question: Next, the psalm talks about strength. True or false: God delights in the strength of the horse.

cards.text: He takes no pleasure in the legs of a man either. Friend, I'm a cookie stamper on a gold base with no legs at ALL, and this is the first time that's ever worked out for me.

cards.question: Not the strength of the horse, not the legs of a man. So who IS the LORD pleased with?

cards.text: Those who fear Him and hope in His loving devotion. Not the fastest or the strongest, just the ones hoping in Him.
Here comes the third call to praise, and this time the psalmist talks straight to the city: "Exalt the LORD, O Jerusalem; praise your God, O Zion!" Then come the reasons why.

cards.question: First reason Jerusalem should praise: God makes something in the city stronger. What is it?
God strengthens the bars of Jerusalem's gates. Who does He bless inside them?
Gates strong, children blessed. Out at Jerusalem's borders, God makes ___.

cards.text: And He fills Jerusalem with the finest wheat. I'm a baker, friend, so that's DOUGH talk, and my eyebrows just hit my hat.
Then the psalm zooms out from one city to the whole earth: God sends forth His command.

cards.question: True or false: the psalm says God's word moves slowly across the earth.

cards.text: Then winter shows up. He spreads the snow like wool and scatters the frost like ashes.

cards.question: Snow like wool, frost like ashes. Then God casts forth His ___ like pebbles.

cards.text: Then the psalmist asks, "Who can withstand His icy blast?" Not me, friend, because my mustache would freeze straight out like a coat rack.

cards.question: Snow, frost and hail everywhere. Then God sends forth His word. What happens to all that cold?

cards.text: He unleashes His winds, and the waters flow. Friend, I've talked to plenty of cold dough, and it has NEVER listened.

cards.question: His word shows up again. Now the psalm says God declares His word, His statutes and judgments, to a people. Who?
God declared His word to Jacob and His statutes and judgments to Israel. True or false: the psalm says He has done this for every nation.

cards.text: He has done this for no other nation, and they do not know His judgments. And the psalm ends right where it started: "Hallelujah!"

rule.text: He calls the baker "baker" or "friend," and talks to one baker at a time. Never "my baker," "kids" or "sweetie."

findings.problem: "From one broken heart" turns the text's plural ("the brokenhearted… their wounds") into a single heart.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The question says "God knows exactly how many stars there are," but v4 says He "determines the number of the stars." Knowing a number is not the same as determining it.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: This story card only restates the answer to card 6 ("Every single star, by NAME") and adds a joke. It tells nothing new from the passage.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: "Naming every star says something about God" makes v4 the reason for v5. The text puts the two verses side by side and leaves their connection open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: "Great is our Lord, and mighty in power" (v5) is never told on any card. The only v5 card is the true or false about His understanding having no limit.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: This story card only restates the answer to card 14 ("The young ravens call, and God feeds them") and adds a joke. It tells nothing new from the passage.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: The setup ("Not the strength of the horse, not the legs of a man") rules out both wrong answers, since "never stumble" and "stand the tallest" are about legs and physical strength. That leaves only the right answer.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "It blows away" can be argued from the same verse, because v18 goes on to say "He unleashes His winds."

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.
